subject: Private deployment: PII routing & audit plan
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Claire Park <claire.park@medicorp.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment: PII routing & audit plan

Hi Claire — thanks again for the call earlier. Wanted to capture the outcomes and next steps so we all have the same thread of record. Key points we agreed:

- Scope: Medicorp will pilot Redwood Private in a VPC located in us-west-2. The pilot scope is EHR-derived ingestion for a single division (claims ingestion). PII elements called out: SSN (hashed on ingest), patient name, DOB, and contact info.
- Network boundary: Traffic originates from Medicorp VPC, goes to a customer-controlled NAT gateway. Redwood Private will be deployed in your VPC via our connector subnet (no public IPs).
- Egress policy: No outbound calls to third-party endpoints are allowed from inference nodes. Only outbound to internal Medicorp endpoints and to Redwood-managed control plane (TLS) on port 443 is permitted; all control-plane interactions will be logged.
- Logs & retention: Audit logs for model inference metadata (request id, timestamp, model id, token counts) retained for 365 days; full prompt logging is optional and must be configured per customer policy.
- Air-gapped concern: You may want an air-gapped variant — discussed an on-prem package; that requires a separate qualification step (network, storage, and ops readiness).

Action items (owners & target dates):
- Medicorp to send PII mapping spreadsheet and network diagram (Claire) — ETA Wed 5/26.
- Redwood (Soogin) to draft a tight list of control points we will need on the Collector/Connector — ETA Fri 5/28.
- Redwood (Marissa) to prepare a short runbook for the pilot, including egress denylist patterns and required IAM roles — ETA Mon 6/1.
- Legal: Medicorp to indicate any mandatory retention windows beyond 365 days (Claire to loop Legal).

Attachments: I’ve attached a sample connector diagram and a PII mapping template we referenced.

Thanks — I’ll follow up once we receive your mapping.

--
Sean Gallagher
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Claire Park <claire.park@medicorp.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Brian Soto <brian.soto@medicorp.com>, Legal (Medicorp) <legal@medicorp.com>
Date: 2027-05-23T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: PII routing & audit plan

Sean — thanks for the summary, that looks right. Quick clarifications from our side after internal sync:

- PII scope refinement: We will not share raw SSNs with Redwood; they will be hashed at ingestion by our preprocessing lambda (we will include the hashing transform in the mapping). For the pilot please treat SSN-related fields as hashed-only; we'll confirm the hashing algorithm in the mapping.
- Residency: All raw artifacts must remain inside our VPC. Derived artifacts (embeddings) can be optionally stored outside if encrypted and approved by Legal — but for the pilot we prefer no external storage.
- Logging: We need at minimum the inference metadata logs (request id, timestamp, model id). Prompt retention is a blocker for Legal unless redaction or customer-side masking is possible; Legal is asking for a config knob to disable full prompt capture per deployment.

We’ll attach the PII mapping and a simplified network diagram by EOD Wed 5/26. Legal asked that Redwood include a short note on where control-plane metadata is stored (and for how long).

Claire Park
Director, Cloud Integrations — Medicorp Health
claire.park@medicorp.com | +1 (503) 555-0114

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Park <claire.park@medicorp.com>
Date: 2027-05-23T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: PII routing & audit plan — security asks and connector details

On May 23, 2027, at 9:07 AM, Claire Park <claire.park@medicorp.com> wrote:
> Sean — thanks for the summary, that looks right. Quick clarifications from our side after internal sync: ...

Thanks Claire — helpful. A few technical confirmations and requests from Redwood Security so we can produce the connector spec and runbook we promised:

1) Hashing confirmation: please confirm the hashing algorithm (SHA-256 salted?) and whether hashing happens in the Lambda before the connector's Collector. If hashing is customer-side pre-collector, Redwood will treat that column as non-PII for pilot handling.

2) Connector network posture: Our recommended deployment pattern for the pilot: connector instances in a private subnet with no internet route, NAT only for outbound to your monitoring endpoints if required. Control plane callbacks (control plane -> customer agent) are one-way secured TLS connections initiated from the customer connector; no inbound from Redwood to connector IPs is required.

3) Prompt retention knob: Redwood Private has a configuration flag at deploy-time to disable prompt capture; when disabled, only inference metadata is emitted. We will document this in the runbook and include sample terraform variables for the pilot.

4) Audit log storage: by default metadata logs are forwarded to an S3 bucket in your account with server-side encryption (AES-256) and lifecycle policy we can recommend (365d by default). If Medicorp requires longer retention we’ll provide guidance for retention policies and an estimate for minimal incremental storage cost.

5) Evidence & SOC-like artifacts: To speed Legal review, I’m attaching a short checklist and the connector architecture (see attachments). I suggest we provide a one-page note on control-plane metadata residency and invite Legal to our next technical sync.

Action: Sean — recommend we schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive next week with Medicorp's infra + Legal. I can present the connector diagram and retention knobs.

--
Soojin Lee
Security & Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-private-connector-arch.pdf, medicorp-pii-mapping-template.xlsx

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-05-24T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: PII routing & audit plan — agreed next steps

Claire / Brian / Legal — appreciate the quick turn. Confirming next steps and who’s doing what:

- Medicorp to share: PII mapping (with hashing algorithm indicated) + network VPC diagram (Claire) — due 2027-05-26 EOD.
- Redwood to produce: 1-page control-plane metadata residency note (Soojin) — due 2027-05-27.
- Redwood to produce: connector spec + pilot runbook (Marissa & Vanessa) — due 2027-05-31.
- Schedule technical deep-dive: Proposed timeslot Tue 5/28 10:00–10:30 PT. Claire, can you confirm? I’ll include Soojin and Marissa.

Notes:
- For the pilot we will default to prompt-capture disabled unless Medicorp explicitly approves it during pilot config. That is a blocking item for Legal; please confirm if Legal will accept metadata-only for the pilot so we can proceed with infra provisioning.
- If Medicorp requires an air-gapped build beyond the VPC connector, that will trigger the on-prem qualification checklist and extend pilot lead time (we’ll estimate at the technical sync).

Thanks — I’ll open a HubSpot task and drop the links to the attachments and the DocuSign route once Legal confirms contract path.

Best,
Sean
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
